chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Two ferocious wolves among a flock of sheep that have been separated from their shepherd, one at the front and one at the back, are not more destructive to it than the love of wealth and status is for the religion of the Muslim.
ai.seo_question: What are the two most destructive forces to a Muslim's religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the vivid metaphor of two wolves attacking a shepherdless flock to illustrate how the love of wealth (*al-mal*) and status (*al-sharaf*) corrupts the religion of a Muslim. This ethical teaching highlights that these two desires are the most damaging internal forces to one's faith, a concept deeply rooted in Shia scholarly tradition as the primary distractions from spiritual purity. The comparison underscores that just as wolves devour the flock, these worldly passions consume the essence of religious devotion when left unchecked.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Two ferocious wolves among sheep who have separated from their shepherd, one being among its front ones and one being among its back ones, are not more damaging among them than the love of the world and the fame would be regarding the Religion of the Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from abu Jamilah from Muhammad al-Halabi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
No two fierce wolves in a flock of sheep without a shepherd, one wolf on either side is as quick (to destroy them) as the love of property and fame is to destroy the religion of a Muslim.”
